drug_name: Antiseptic Cleansing Wipe (0.9% Sodium Chloride / Normal Saline)
what_its_for: These wipes are used to gently clean and rinse skin around wounds, cuts, scrapes, or medical devices such as IV sites, catheter insertion points, or feeding tube sites. The 0.9% sodium chloride (normal saline) solution matches the natural salt level in your body, making it very gentle on skin and tissue. It helps remove dirt, debris, and bacteria without causing irritation or stinging.
how_to_take: 1. Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water before using the wipe. 2. Open the individual packet carefully and unfold the wipe. 3. Gently wipe the skin or wound area using a clean, circular motion moving from the center outward, OR wipe in one direction only — do not scrub back and forth. 4. Allow the area to air dry or gently pat dry with a clean gauze pad. 5. Dispose of the used wipe immediately in the trash — do not flush. 6. Never reuse a wipe. Each wipe is for single use only. 7. Wash your hands again after finishing.
dosing: Use as directed by your doctor, nurse, or wound care specialist. In general, these wipes can be used 1 to 3 times per day or each time you change a dressing or clean a wound site. There is no specific dose in the traditional sense since this is a topical cleansing product. Follow the instructions provided by your healthcare team for your specific situation.
missed_dose: If you forget to clean your wound or skin site at the usual time, go ahead and clean it as soon as you remember. Then return to your normal cleaning schedule. Do not 'double up' by using extra wipes to make up for a missed cleaning unless your healthcare provider tells you to. If you are unsure, call your doctor or nurse for guidance.
storage: Store individual wipe packets at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep them away from direct sunlight, heat sources, and humidity. Do not freeze. Keep packets sealed until ready to use — an open or dried-out wipe should be thrown away. Keep all wipes out of reach of children and pets. Check the expiration date printed on the package before use and discard any expired wipes.
what_to_avoid: • Do not use these wipes on eyes or inside the mouth unless specifically directed by your doctor. • Do not use on deep puncture wounds, serious burns, or animal bites without first consulting your healthcare provider. • Do not use if the packet seal is already broken or the wipe appears dried out. • Avoid using wipes that contain alcohol or other added antiseptics unless your doctor recommends them — saline wipes are meant to be gentle. • Do not use the same wipe on more than one area of the body or on more than one person. • Avoid flushing used wipes down the toilet as they can clog pipes.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor or healthcare provider if you notice any of the following: • Increased redness, warmth, or swelling around the wound or skin site. • Pus, foul odor, or unusual discharge from the wound. • The wound is not healing or appears to be getting worse. • You develop a fever of 100.4°F (38°C) or higher. • You experience increasing pain around the wound area. • You notice a skin rash or allergic reaction after using the wipes, such as hives, itching, or swelling. • The wound area becomes numb or changes color (very pale, blue, or black).
when_it_works: Saline cleansing wipes work immediately upon contact with the skin. They begin to physically remove dirt, bacteria, and debris right away as you wipe. You may notice the area looks and feels cleaner right after use. Since saline matches your body's own fluids, it supports the natural healing process with each use over time. Wound healing itself depends on many factors including wound size, your overall health, and how consistently you follow your wound care routine.
special_populations: Babies and Children: Saline wipes are generally safe and gentle for use on infants and children. Always follow your pediatrician's specific instructions for wound care in young children. Elderly Patients: Older adults often have thinner, more fragile skin. Use extra gentle pressure when wiping to avoid skin tears. Pregnant or Breastfeeding Women: Normal saline is considered safe during pregnancy and breastfeeding when used on the skin as directed. Patients with Diabetes: Diabetic patients should monitor wound sites very closely as wounds may heal more slowly. Contact your doctor right away if any wound shows signs of infection. Patients with Kidney Disease: Saline wipes used on the skin are generally safe, but discuss any concerns with your healthcare provider.
